summary: The focused gates pass, but Review B found trust, provenance, replay, and transaction-boundary defects.

findings.title: Cross-organization source identities can be replayed under another organization.
evidence: The memory key combines the current organization and idempotency key.
The database uniqueness keys combine mastery tenant and idempotency or source attempt.
A second organization with its own principal can submit the first organization's sourceAttemptId and idempotencyKey and receive applied status.
The direct probe returned crossOrganizationReuse=applied.
findings.impact: The required cross-organization replay and evidence-reuse denial is not enforced.
findings.required_fix: Bind source attempts and idempotency identities to a trusted organization-owned source record or enforce a global immutable origin registry.

findings.title: The projection accepts claims without Sales role or canonical organization authorization.
evidence: The local schema requires ACTIVE status and aud=sales, but it does not require SALES_REP or SALES_ADMIN.
The local schema accepts any valid organization key.
The existing resolveSalesCompanyPrincipal path rejects non-internal organizations and roleless identities.
The direct probe resolved a tenant for an empty role list and other-company organization key.
findings.impact: A structurally valid but unauthorized identity can create a mapping and project mastery evidence.
findings.required_fix: Require the trusted Company Identity principal result and enforce the exact Sales role and organization policy before mapping.

findings.title: The projection does not validate reviewed activity bindings or roleplay consent.
evidence: The payload checks only three nonblank strings and a score range.
The implementation does not load or validate the accepted Sales bindings package.
The implementation does not validate attempt immutability, evaluator provenance, consent, or retention status.
A payload with sales.unknown.objective, sales.unknown.variant, and unapproved-rubric returned applied status.
The Phase 1 acceptance marks all roleplays pending until an approved evaluator and immutable-attempt verifier exist.
findings.impact: A2 fails, and unapproved or non-consented evidence can mutate KST/SRS state.
findings.required_fix: Validate the exact activity binding and attempt record before projection, then require the consent and retention gate for roleplay evidence.

findings.title: Receipt columns are not bound to the referenced outbox row in PostgreSQL.
evidence: The receipt table has a single-column outbox foreign key.
The receipt organization, tenant, learner, and idempotency columns have no composite foreign key or consistency check against the outbox row.
The adapter treats receipt existence for an outbox ID as completion.
findings.impact: A direct database writer can attach a foreign organization or learner projection receipt to an outbox row.
findings.required_fix: Add a composite receipt-to-outbox foreign key and matching checks for organization, tenant, learner, and idempotency identity.

findings.title: Outbox creation, mastery commit, and receipt insertion are not one atomic transaction.
evidence: ensureOutbox commits its transaction before the Mastery adapter runs.
The Mastery commit and receipt insert run in separate operations.
A process failure between the Mastery commit and receipt insert leaves an applied commit without a Sales receipt.
findings.impact: The Finance-proven atomic outbox contract is not met, and recovery depends on a later retry.
findings.required_fix: Use one shared transaction boundary for the outbox, Mastery commit, and receipt, or add a durable delivery state with an atomic commit protocol.

findings.title: Historical migrations were edited instead of receiving an additive repair migration.
evidence: The live PostgreSQL 16 chain now passes after nested breakpoints were removed.
The source changes alter migrations that may already exist in deployed databases.
No new migration records the repair for databases that already applied those migration tags.
findings.impact: New databases and existing databases can have different historical migration bytes.
findings.required_fix: Use a serial additive repair migration or record an explicit compatibility decision for already-applied databases.
